core_obligations: Use that L has characteristic p to represent M as an Artin-Schreier extension, choose z not in L with xi = z^p - z in L, and pick n >= 0 minimal with pi^n xi in B; conclude for n = 0 that M/L is unramified with respect to B (proof lines 34833-34839).

Derive the perfectness of kappa_A from assumption (4) and choose compatible Cohen maps kappa_A -> A/pi^n A and kappa_B -> B/pi^n B, lifting the second to a map of sets sigma : kappa_B -> B (proof lines 34842-34848).
Expand xi as sum_{i=n..1} sigma(lambda_i) pi^{-i} + b and split {n, ..., 1} into the sets I and J according to whether lambda_i lies in kappa_A (proof lines 34849-34861).

Settle the case J empty: show that p does not divide n, since otherwise the explicit rewriting of a = a_0^p + pi a_1 inside the Artin-Schreier expression would contradict minimality of n, then form K_1 by w^p - w = pi^{-n}a and trace the resulting L_1, B_1 and M_1 through the characteristic p lemma to produce the weak solution (proof lines 34864-34894).

For the induction on the size of J, show that if j' = p^r j with j, j' in J one may replace z by the displayed z' so that the new coefficient lambda'_j vanishes while all other coefficients are unchanged, strictly decreasing J (proof lines 34898-34918).
Assuming no such pair exists, write each lambda_j for j in J as mu_j^{p^{r_j}} with mu_j not a p-th power and let j be the unique index maximizing j p^{-r_j} (proof lines 34921-34924).

Choose r > max(r_j + 1) with j p^{r - r_j} > n and a separable extension K_1/K totally ramified with respect to A of degree p^r whose valuation ring A_1 has uniformizer pi' with (pi')^{p^r} = pi + pi^{n+1} a, then check L_1 = L tensor_K K_1 is a field totally ramified over B (proof lines 34925-34933).

Recompute xi in the integral closure B_1 in the displayed two-part form, use that the coefficients with index in I are p^r-th powers modulo (pi')^{n p^r}, and perform the second explicit change of z given by the displayed align to obtain (z')^p - z' = sum_I x_i (pi')^{-i} + sum_J sigma(mu_j) (pi')^{-j p^{r-r_j}} + b'_1 (proof lines 34934-34968).

Conclude that the maximal exponent j p^{r - r_j} is unique, exceeds every i in I and is divisible by p, so that M_1/L_1 falls into case (C) of the characteristic p lemma, finishing the proof (proof lines 34969-34973).
difficulty_reason: The lemma works with a tower A in B in C of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L in M, assumes A in B weakly unramified, characteristic of K equal to p, M a degree p Galois extension of L, and kappa_A equal to the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, and concludes the existence of a finite Galois extension K_1/K, totally ramified with respect to A, that is a weak solution for A -> C (source lines 34817-34830). The proof is a genuine multi-stage induction. It first uses that the characteristic p extension is Artin-Schreier, picks z with xi = z^p - z in L and chooses n minimal with pi^n xi in B, disposing of n = 0 as unramified (proof lines 34833-34839). It then invokes the perfectness of kappa_A together with the Cohen map to write xi as a sum over powers of pi with coefficients in kappa_B and splits the index set into the parts I and J according to whether the coefficient lies in kappa_A (proof lines 34842-34861). The proof then runs a first induction on the size of J: the case J empty is handled by a p-divisibility argument showing p does not divide n, then constructing K_1 with w^p - w = pi^{-n} a and tracking the extension through L_1, B_1, M_1 to conclude (proof lines 34864-34894); the induction step replaces the chosen z by an explicit z' that kills the coefficient of the offending index, shrinking J (proof lines 34898-34918). Finally it writes each remaining lambda_j as a proper p^{r_j}-th power, picks the unique maximal j p^{-r_j}, constructs a degree p^r extension with uniformizer controlled by (pi')^{p^r} = pi + pi^{n+1}a, recomputes xi in the integral closure B_1, performs a second explicit change of z, and reads the conclusion off case (C) of the characteristic p lemma (proof lines 34921-34973). The two nested inductions and the two explicit changes of the Artin-Schreier generator are independent research-level content, not routine bookkeeping.
